symptom: An import mapping's custom object handler `find … by M.MF ( P: member )` that fed a JSON member to a microflow parameter of an incompatible type (a String member into an Integer parameter) passed `check` and `exec` and was written; `mx check` reported CE0282 "The microflow parameter 'P' is of type 'Integer'. It does not match the specified type 'String'".
file: mdl/executor/validate_mapping_handler_types.go ValidateMappingHandlerTypes (MDL107), called from validate_program.go with the lazy project opener. Tests: validate_mapping_handler_types_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-handler-param-type-mismatch.fail.mdl and the clean control mapping-handler-types.mdl
cause: buildCustomHandler binds each parameter to its member and never compares the member's JSON type with the parameter's declared type.
insight: **The compatibility matrix is small enough to measure whole, which made a name-based lookup safe where a path-following one was not.** 25 pairings of {String, Integer, Long, Decimal, Boolean, DateTime} x {string, integer, decimal, boolean, date-time} members, one project each on MxBuild 11.16.1: a String parameter takes everything, Decimal also takes Integer, Long takes Integer, the rest only their own type. The rule finds the member by its NAME in the whole structure and judges only when every occurrence is one known value type, so it never has to follow the handler's element path through arrays and two-level items (the duplication that made a CE0281 mirror a drift risk); a name that is absent or typed differently in two places is left to the build. The cost is silence on that ambiguous case, which is the right direction to be wrong in.
